_about: How many copies of each world-effects template the stage builds — the effect-template pool (BL-225). Each PlayEffectAt call takes the next copy, so that many overlapping calls to one effect keep their own trails/smoke at their own sites instead of collapsing onto the last one. Hand-authored engine config, NOT extracted game data: the original instances a fresh copy per CALL_ANIMATION and has no such number, so every value here is our finite approximation of 'unbounded'. Consumed by src/Session/EffectPools.cs (M3 polish-5 D10).
_references: The mechanism and its traps: docs/architecture.md (AnimRuntime's pool paragraph, WorldEffectsFactory). The tuning entry: backlog.md BL-231. The root names are WorldEffectsFactory.EffectStageRoots — a name here that is not a stage root is reported, never guessed.
_sizing: slots = min(maxSlots, base + perExtraPlayer x (players - 1)). Splitscreen/multiplayer multiplies the sources: every extra aircraft is another gun and another rocket at its own site, so the per-player term is what keeps a 4-player or 16-player session from collapsing back onto one copy. maxSlots is the memory guard — each slot is one more copy of that root's subtree.
_instrument: AnimRuntime.PoolRecycles counts every call that wrapped onto a still-live slot, and the runtime names the first wrap per effect ('anim: effect pool for <name> recycled slot N of M'). A scripted run that logs none had enough pool; raise the root that logs one, not the default.

default.why: Sized against rocket concurrency: FIRE_RATE 1/s against ~2.5 s of authored trail motion means at most 3 overlapping blasts per aircraft, plus one spare. Measured: a 9-rocket burst at 1/s logged zero recycles.

gunhit.why: The gun-impact family stays SHARED on purpose (C8): gun hits are throttled to one play per 0.1 s per effect name and each instance is bounded to 0.3 s, so consecutive hits reuse one relocated copy by design at ten hits a second. Raising this without removing that throttle buys copies nothing will use. Removing the throttle is its own step, with its own emitter-count check.

dum_gunhit.why: As gunhit — the dum/ap variants' template root.

mag_gunhit.why: As gunhit — the magnesium variants' template root.

partial_damage_obj.why: The two DAMAGE_SEQUENCE sputters (sputter_black_smoke_obj / sputter_fire_smoke_obj) live here, and damage-stage smoke is the genuinely many-at-once case: one salvo into a cluster damages several objects in the same frame, each wanting its own emitter on its own object. Measured — five simultaneous ap_h2otwr kills wrapped a 4-slot pool exactly once.

_localCallAbout: A SEPARATE, smaller pool for death-triggered CALL_ANIMATION targets that anchor on a 'library root' gamez node (docs/formats/gamez.md; AnimRuntime.ResolveLibraryRoot, BL-253) — kept apart from 'roots' above because that map is validated against WorldEffectsFactory.EffectStageRoots (an unknown key there warns) and these names never are one. Sizing is the SAME three-layer answer as the effects pool: (1) pool MEMBERSHIP is the data-driven parentless-root rule, no config involved; (2) pool SIZE prefers the gamez's OWN authored duplicate count where the node list ships one — several effect templates do (sonic_ring/sonic_flare x5, mb1/mb_spinflame x5, zep_skin_fire1-4, yellow_spark_01/_02, flame_ball_01-_03, fire_here/fire_here2, muzzle_burst/muzzle_burst2 — verified same-shape single-child records, docs/formats/gamez.md), in which case N IS the original's own answer and belongs nowhere but the census; (3) 'localCallRoots' below is ONLY for a template that ships exactly one gamez record (facdsticks: single record, confirmed) yet is observed running several copies at once in the original (BL-253's CAP-24 A/B, 2026-08-04) — there the original cloned dynamically and the count genuinely is NOT decodable, so it is a TUNE entry same as the rest of this file, tracked in backlog.md's BL-231 list. No perExtraPlayer term: these are world geometry, not per-player ordnance, and WorldSession does not carry a player count at this layer.

localCallDefault.why: A library-root template with no entry here stays single-copy (today's behaviour) unless explicitly raised — matches genx12, which is deliberately NOT pooled in this pass (kkgate is one propane tank per chapter, never overlapping itself).

_crashAbout: A THIRD pool, for the per-player crash rig's templates (BL-288) — kept apart from 'roots' (the WORLD stage's, validated against its derived root set) and 'localCallRoots' (library-root clones). The rig's damage-stage menu (pdpanel1..8, player_damage_trail, the random_gun_impact shims, both crash defs) CALLs each template from several distinct anchors — a panel, prop1, a wreck piece — and the one shared copy was relocated-and-restarted onto every new call site, discarding the previous site's burst mid-flight. Unlike the world pool there is no cursor: AnimRuntime.AssignCallerSlot pins each (root, call anchor) pair to its own slot on first call, so sizes below are the AUTHORED distinct-anchor counts read off the C1 cam_anim defs (2026-08-06), not TUNE guesses — a re-count is only owed if the shared damage-stage defs ever change. No perExtraPlayer term: the whole rig is built once per player already. A root with no entry stays single-copy (the crash choreography templates, played once per crash).

crashDefault.why: Single copy = the pre-BL-288 behaviour, correct for every template only ever called from one anchor at a time (the crash choreography's splash/fire/steam family).

planeflakes.why: gimmeflakes debris — called AT its own pdpN by all eight pdpanelN defs; one copy per panel.

short_firetrail.why: Panel burn — pdpanel1/2/4/5/6 WITH their pdpN, plus player_damage_trail WITH prop1.

large_firetrail.why: pdpanel4/6 WITH their pdpN, plus the crash defs' four WITH pieceN trails — which shared one copy across all four flung pieces before this pool existed.

flame_ball_02.why: small_fireball — pdpanel7/8 (the world's own flame_ball callers play on the world-effects runtime, not this rig).

yellow_spark_02.why: yellow_sparks_follow — pdpanel5 plus random_gun_impact's three WITH pdp1/2/4 shim calls.

facdsticks.why: C2's facade panels (fcpan01-39) each CALL_ANIMATION facade_parts, whose template facdsticks ships as exactly ONE gamez record — no authored duplicate count to read off. The original's own parallel debris (BL-253's CAP-24 A/B, 2026-08-04: several broken panels' four-log sets airborne at once) proves it clones the template at runtime, a count this format cannot supply. 6 is TUNE, not measured: a facade row at flight speed breaks panels roughly 0.2-0.5 s apart with each set's flight lasting 4-5 s, so a row of 8-10 panels can have 8-10 sets in the air; 6 covers most flight-through passes without recycling, at the cost of eventually wrapping (evicting the oldest still-flying set) on a longer burst. Revisit against an in-cockpit measurement of how many panels a real pass breaks.
